newsitem.title: FINLAND: VALMET WINS FIM 20 MLN AUTOMATION DEALS. [CORRECTED 11:30 GMT]
newsitem.headline: VALMET WINS FIM 20 MLN AUTOMATION DEALS. [CORRECTED 11:30 GMT]

text.p: Finnish paper machine group Valmet said in a statement on Thursday it had won automation orders from UPM-Kymmene and Metsa-Botnia worth a total of nearly 20 million markka.

The value of the Metsa-Botnia order for automation of a lye line process control system was about 10 million markka and the value of UPM-Kymmene's order for a process control system rebuild was about eight million markka, it said.
(Company corrects the value of the order).
Metsa-Botnia is owned by UPM and Metsa-Serla . Its order was for its Joutseno Pulp pulp mill, Valmet said.

"The order is Valmet Automation's first process control system order from Joutseno Pulp," it said, adding it would generate about 20 person-hour years of work for Valmet Automation's unit in Tampere. The new line will start up in early 1999.

UPM's process control rebuild order was for a coating control kitchen and sludge plant control system at UPM's Jamsankoski paper mill; the rebuilt system will be taken into use at the turn of the year.
